why: All from anatomical position (standing, palms forward). Supination: palm forward (or up, scooping soup), radius and ulna parallel; pronation: palm back, the radius crosses over the ulna in an X. Flexion: bending, the angle between the bones gets smaller; extension: it gets bigger. Abduction: away from the midline; adduction: back toward it. Medial (internal) rotation: the front of the arm or thigh turns toward the midline; lateral (external) rotation: away from it. Dorsiflexion: the top of the foot moves toward the shin; plantar flexion: toes point down. Inversion: the sole turns toward the midline; eversion: away from it (these happen below the ankle, in the tarsal joints). Circumduction: one end stays put while the other draws a circle (the hand, with the shoulder still). Opposition: the thumb tip touches a fingertip of the same hand.
